giveaway: The dash barely travels on screen and keeps an upright silhouette: make it a long, low, leaning lunge with the afterimages stretched along the path.
Only the sword arm snaps into a stiff held pose: move the whole body too (recoil, a backward weight shift, a step, the free arm flaring) before the guard settles.

From frames 4-15 the body locks into a single forward lean with the arm pointed stiffly ahead and the legs barely moving: a low push-off, then let the legs stride or skid and the trailing arm swing, then rise back toward stance instead of holding one pose.

The sword freezes in a vertical high guard while the free arm sticks straight out (a T-pose): snap the blade diagonal across the body in 2-3 frames, tuck the off-hand by the hilt, brace the knees, a short recoil, then settle.

Frames 5-17 still read as one hunched pose folded at the waist with the free arm hanging in front: lean the whole body from the ankles, swing the free arm back to trail, and scissor or skid the legs clearly.

The blade reaches a good diagonal by frames 3-6 but the body below the arms never reacts: drop the hips into a braced crouch at contact with a sharp 3-4 frame recoil of blade and shoulders, then settle.
After the opening flash fades, only the small key hint by the blade says the window is still open: keep a visible glow or pulse on the player or blade for the whole window.
The flash step's white afterimages bloomed over the whole frame at impact, hiding the blade connecting (since toned down: plain copies, a narrower cut).

Two fresh judges (round 1: 2 to 7; after holding the halo and ring to the end and lightening the body tint, round 2: 3 to 7, flat): the even blue fill flattens the body; a rim light or outline that keeps its shading, brightening as the window closes.
Round 1, a lean from the ankles, and round 2, a held wide split, both scored 5 to 4 and were reverted: pass 94's keys stay, and only the lower foot now stays on the floor. Flat at 5: a stalled loop.

Three fresh judges, HEAD 3 against ours 5, 4, then 5 on the final build (the blade knocked out and back, the body sinking over it): frames 5-9 hold one crouched pose; drive hands and chest back and up at frames 3-4, then ease forward with a damped overshoot and a knee dip.

Round 1, a Blender-authored clip (IK feet, real contacts): the legs stay folded under the hips while the torso dives flat; the reference splits wide, back leg straight, lead foot planted far ahead, then lands wide and low.
Round 2, a wide split and a low skid: reads as a deep squat close to a kneel, knees tucked, the cape and ghosts lying flat like a prone slide.

Round 3, hips raised so the legs straighten: one stiff leaning plank, legs close together, the recovery upright and narrow. 4, 4, 3 against the old 3, 5, 5: flat, the clip is not adopted (branch wip/p101-dash-clip).

Aleix's last try, a deep lunge (front thigh level, back leg straight far behind, hips half a metre up), strip drawn every step and closer: judge 1, "lies almost flat like a tipped-over board, jumps back to standing by frames 9-10".
Judge 2: the push-off reads well but the torso never gets as low and sprawled as the reference, and frames 8-9 jump from a deep crouch to upright with no settle.
Judge 3: no load-up before the near-horizontal lunge of frame 2, and it pops upright from frame 9 to 10. 3, 3, 5 against 4, 5, 4: not adopted (wip/p102-dash-lunge); the dash stops at 5.
